title: Three Winters and One Short Stone
subtitle: 神话信仰 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 神话信仰（人与社会·历史社会与文化·神话与信仰）
meta: 主题语境：神话信仰（人与社会·历史社会与文化·神话与信仰）　|　核心词汇：god　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 god 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the storyteller ① praised a god that no elder in the village would have described, and he said the praising was the whole of the winter. The ② god, meaning the figure itself and not the stone, ran three winters and stayed undescribed in the book; a god, he said, is the only thing in a village that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ god in that village had the same short lamp beside it, and the ④ god at the far shrine, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A god, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the storyteller said the describing is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the god was the whole of the matter, meaning the mercy and not the figure. The ⑥ god, meaning the mercy and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; god, he said, is either something you praise or the only word that means both a figure and a mercy. He said the mercy is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ god had become a line in a song, and the song had become an argument about the short lamp. The ⑧ god of the whole thing, the storyteller wrote in November, was one village and three winters of describing; god, he said, is either the one at the far shrine or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ god I remember is the one described in the song, which closed in 1963 and is still described as the quietest in the village. A ⑩ god, my mother said in 1965, is the only one that improves by being described; every god, she said, is a mercy that has agreed to look like a figure. She said the mercy was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 神（指村里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 神（指那个形象本身，与石头相对）
C. 固定搭配：praise a god 赞颂一位神
D. n. 神（指留给孩子们敬的那一位）
E. n. 神（抽象总称，指一个村子的敬神之事）
F. n. 神（指歌里写到、被记下的那一位）
G. n. 神恩；庇佑（指一件事里人人都求却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 庇佑（抽象总称，指人人都求却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: praised a god that no elder in the village would have described
The god, meaning the figure itself and not the stone
the god at the far shrine
the god was the whole of the matter

The god of the whole thing

answers.why: praise a god 意为“赞颂一位神”，1957 年那位说书人赞颂了村里没有一位长者肯描述的一位神。
god 意为“神”，指那个形象本身而不是石头，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被描述。
god 意为“神”，指村里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一盏矮矮的油灯。
god 意为“神”，指最远那座神龛里留给孩子们敬的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
god 意为“神恩、庇佑”，指一件事里人人都求却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份庇佑就是那件事的全部。
god 意为“庇佑”，指人人都求却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位神，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
god 意为“神”，指歌里写到、被记下的那一位，到 1961 年这一位成了歌里的一行。
god 意为“神”，说书人十一月写道，整件事的敬神之事是一个村子和三个冬天的描述。
god 意为“神”，我记得的是歌里描述过的那一位，1963 年唱完了，至今仍被说成村里最安静的一位。
god 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，一位神是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
